title: Queueing impact analysis for multi-class arrival harness
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build and run a focused load-testing harness that isolates queueing effects under mixed-priority traffic. The goal is to quantify how continuous batching and request queue dynamics interact with multi-class arrivals (foreground low-latency vs. background high-throughput) and to produce stable metrics for tokens/sec, p95/p99 latencies, and regression detection thresholds. Deliverables: 1) reproducible harness (LoadForge) with configurable arrival distributions and priority preemption; 2) dashboards with control-chart based regression alerts; 3) a gang of experiments across model sizes, KV cache warm states, and batching window settings; 4) recommendations for autoscaler and routing policies that minimize tail regressions while preserving token throughput.
comments: 2026-02-21: Proto harness (LoadForge v0.1) created by Aisha. Supports Poisson and bursty arrival generators; basic priority tagging implemented.

2026-02-24: Initial run against dev-runtime-1.20 revealed p95 spikes when background traffic > 2x foreground; hypothesis: batching window dilation causes head-of-line blocking. Collected token/sec traces and per-priority latency histograms.
2026-02-27: Discussion with Marta Díaz (SRE) — added KV cache warm/cold toggles and a warmup phase to avoid startup noise. Also added a 'priority drain' mode to simulate graceful preemption.
2026-03-01: Liam implemented control-chart based regression detector (EWMA + thresholding) in metrics-collector; hooked into alerting channel. PR #421 opened for review.
2026-03-03: Design feedback from PM Ravi Patel: include a synthetic client that mimics query-length variance (short/long tokens) and record kernel-selection logs for correlation analysis.

2026-03-05: Running full factorial experiments (batch_window_ms x autoscaler_threshold x bg:fg ratios). Partial results uploaded to dashboard; p95 regressions correlate strongly with increased queued request variance, not average throughput. Next: run on dedicated cluster (staging-dedicated-3) to validate at higher concurrency.
